text: {Job Begins to Argues His Case} d "Look, I've seen everything; I've listened carefully and I understand.
What you know, I know, too; I'm not inferior to you.
But I want to talk to the Almighty; and I'm determined to argue my case {The Heb. lacks my case} before God."
{Job Accuses His Friends} d "But as for you, you whitewash with lies; all of you are worthless quacks. {Lit. physicians}
I wish you'd all just shut up. Then at least you would appear to be wise.
"Now listen to my dispute! Pay attention to my arguments. {Lit. arguments of my lips}
Why do you speak falsely on God's behalf and speak deceitfully {Or treachery} about him?
Will you show partiality to him? {Lit. lift up his face} Will you plead God's case?
Will things go well for you under his cross-examination? Can you lie to him, as you would to a human being? {Lit. mankind}
"He will be sure to rebuke you, if you show partiality {Lit. you lift up the face} in secret.
His splendor will petrify you with terror, paralyzing you with fear, won't it?
Your maxims are just worthless proverbs; your defensive arguments are made of clay."
{Job Resolves to Present His Case} d "Don't talk to me! It's my turn to speak; then whatever happens, happens.
Why shouldn't I bite my flesh or take my life in my hands?
Even though he kills me, I'll continue to hope in him. At least I'll be able to argue my case {Or way} to his face!
I have this as my salvation: the godless person won't be appearing before him.
Pay attention {Lit. listen, to listen} to what I have to say and listen to my testimony with your own ears."
{Job Presents His Conditions} d "Look, now! I've prepared my case for court. {Or judgment} I know that I'm going to win. {Lit. I'm in the right}
Who can oppose me? If they do, I'll be silent and die.
Grant me only two things as you deal with me; then I won't hide from you. {Lit. from your face}
Withdraw your hand far from me and keep me from being petrified with terror.
Then call and I'll answer, or let me speak and then you reply to me!"
{Job Presents Himself for Cross-Examination} d "How many of my iniquities and sins have you counted? Show me my transgression and sin.
Why do you hide your face and regard me as your enemy?
Are you a god who would make a leaf tremble or who would prosecute a dry straw?
You've accused me of bitter things; you've caused me to reap {Lit. inherit} the sins of my youth.
You've locked my feet in stocks; you watch all my steps; You've limited where I can walk. {Lit. limited the soles of my feet}
So I'm a man who wears out like something rotten, like a garment that has become moth-eaten."
